summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence was admitted to the surgery service with abdominal bloating/pain, nausea without vomiting, and recurrent hypoglycemia while continuing metronidazole for chronic small intestinal bacterial overgrowth. Evaluation in the ED included abdominal radiography showing a normal bowel gas pattern without obstruction or free air but with moderate fecal loading, and a right upper quadrant ultrasound showing no cholelithiasis or cholecystitis. She was found to have a urinary tract infection and was treated with oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Endocrinology was consulted for hypoglycemia and identified difficulty using her continuous glucose monitor; she was counseled to treat declining glucose trends before the device alarms. Her abdominal discomfort was managed with oral analgesics, tube feeds were continued, and oral intake was restricted to liquids. She remained stable and was discharged home ambulatory with instructions to complete antibiotics, continue metronidazole and tube feeds, monitor glucose closely with earlier sugar intake, and follow up with her outpatient clinicians including her psychologist/therapist.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
